stories.event: The US–Iran war has no ceasefire in place; Iran declared the Islamabad Memorandum void in July and the IRGC declared the Strait of Hormuz closed on 26 October 2026, extending its tanker blockade to the Gulf of Oman on 27 October. On 26–27 October Saudi, Pakistani and Turkish delegations met Iran's leadership in Tehran, and Pakistan's army chief Field Marshal Asim Munir carried a Trump-backed proposal whose terms have not been published. The four governments agreed only to 'continue the dialogue', and as of 28 October Tehran had not announced its answer. Trump has said the US will not attack Iran before the 3 November midterms, and The National reported diplomacy is effectively paused until then. Iran restated on 28 October that Hormuz could reopen within days if the US lifts its naval blockade.

stories.event: The US midterm elections are on 3 November 2026, and nearly 33 million pre-election votes had been cast by 27 October (UF Election Lab). On 26 October federal prosecutors in Washington state wrote to Secretary of State Steve Hobbs alleging that 405 noncitizens are on the voter rolls and demanding their ballots be sequestered by noon on 28 October, warning the United States would otherwise 'seek emergency relief'; Hobbs disputes the list. The Justice Department followed the same pattern in California, where it sued to block tabulation of about 20,000 ballots, and on 22 October it sued pre-emptively to block certification of Alaska's Senate result if Republican Dan Sullivan narrowly loses. Judges in California (David Carter) and Alaska (Sharon Gleason) are expected to rule before election day.

Analysts expect growth of about 0.1% q/q; the Bundesbank expects a noticeable pick-up in the fourth quarter.

stories.event: Israelis voted in a Knesset election on Tuesday 27 October 2026, with turnout of 77.7%, the highest since 1999. TV exit polls put Netanyahu's bloc at 50 seats and Gadi Eisenkot's opposition bloc at 52–53, but the actual count reversed the picture. More than half a million double-envelope ballots (soldiers and voters away from their stations) are being counted from 28 October evening until about Thursday or Friday. The election committee publishes official results on 4 November, after which President Herzog consults party leaders on a prime-ministerial nominee.

stories.event: Mandates of four UN-backed operations — the UN Verification Mission in Colombia, MINURSO in Western Sahara, UNSMIL in Libya and the EUFOR Althea/NATO authorisation in Bosnia and Herzegovina — expire on Saturday 31 October 2026, so the Security Council is expected to vote on renewals on Friday 30 October. stories.event: The Bank of Japan's Policy Board meets on 29–30 October 2026 and announces its decision around noon Tokyo time on Friday 30 October, together with its quarterly Outlook Report. On 18 September it raised the policy rate by 25bp to 1.25%, the highest in 31 years, on a 7-2 vote, with board members Toichiro Asada and Ayano Sato opposing the hike. Board member Hajime Takata has proposed a higher rate at every hold meeting in 2026 (January, March, April, July), joined in April by Naoki Tamura and Junko Nakagawa. The vote split will show whether the board's hawks keep pushing for faster tightening.

stories.event: Since 1 October 2026 the Czech government has capped retail prices of standard petrol and diesel, with the finance ministry announcing a maximum price every working day at 14:00 for the next day, and cut the diesel excise duty to the EU minimum. The cap equals a three-day moving average of four wholesale price indices plus a regulated CZK 2.50 margin and VAT. On 26 October the cabinet extended both measures to 30 November under a new decree from 1 November. The diesel cap has risen as Brent climbed above USD 115 a barrel, reaching CZK 49.46 per litre for 28–29 October after a 50-haléř jump, while the petrol cap has drifted down to CZK 44.45. On Friday 30 October the ministry sets the cap for the weekend.
